title: Understanding Loss Functions
text: The average squared loss is often used in regression problems, but it might not be suitable for classification tasks. Consider how the nature of classification differs from regression.

title: Properties of Cross-Entropy Loss
text: Cross-entropy loss is particularly useful for classification problems because it measures the difference between two probability distributions. Think about how this property might be advantageous.

title: Gradient Descent and Loss Functions
text: Consider how the choice of loss function affects the optimization process, particularly when using gradient descent. How might the properties of cross-entropy loss facilitate this process?

hintAnswer: $$Cross-entropy$$ loss is preferred because it provides a smoother gradient for optimization and better captures the probabilistic nature of classification.
title: Comparing Loss Functions
text: Why might cross-entropy loss be preferred over squared loss for binary classification?
choices: $$Cross-entropy$$ loss is preferred because it provides a smoother gradient for optimization and better captures the probabilistic nature of classification.
